data.title: Gemini CEO Tyler Winklevoss Says Zcash 'Is Not A Lighthouse,' Rejects Public-Good Case For Grants Committee
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tyler Winklevoss said the Zcash Community Grants committee was unnecessary, and that private markets would do a better job of funding development.
  • His comments came as proposals to reduce or eliminate the committee’s 8% share of block rewards stacking up have been making rounds among the community.
  • The grants committee has offered to return some of its treasury, but critics say it doesn’t go far enough.

Zcash (ZEC) is not economically defined as a public good, Gemini (GEMI) co-founder Tyler Winklevoss said on Friday, adding that its development should be funded by the market, not its grants committee.

In a response on X to L. Amber O’Hearn, former member of the Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) committee, Winklevoss rejected the argument that Zcash was a public good and social good that shouldn't be captured by private interests. The exchange is the newest move in a growing fight for the ZEC, which Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) controls.

Economists call a public good non-rivalrous, Winklevoss said, “If you buy 1 ZEC, it’s yours and no one else can't (sic) have it, and if you want to participate in/use the Zcash network, you have to pay for it.” It must be non-excludable, meaning no one can be denied from using it.

Winklevoss said Zcash fails on both points. A holder’s coins are that holder’s alone, he wrote, and anyone wanting to use the network has to pay. “No free-riding,” he said.

Market Over Committee

Winklevoss said he agreed that Zcash was open to everyone and good for society. He said that was not what economists meant by the term, which describes something private markets can’t supply well. “It is not a lighthouse or national defense,” he wrote.

That, he added, meant Zcash did not need what he called a “government-like plundering/taxing mechanism” such as ZCG. He added that it was funded without representation. “The market will handle this and handle it better in all respects,” he said.

He also dismissed O’Hearn’s warning that Zcash could end up within reach of only the rich. He said access was widening fast through wallet and exchange support and through exposure via public companies and exchange-traded funds.

Winklevoss is also a co-founder of Cypherpunk Technologies (CYPH), a Nasdaq-listed company that owns approximately 294,700 ZEC. Winklevoss Asset Services, which earlier this month filed for a spot Zcash ETF to be traded under the ticker WINK.

ZEC’s price was trading at $1,270, up over 1% in the last 24 hours, amid broader market weakness. On Stocktwits, ZEC was one of the top trending tickers in cryptocurrencies at the time of writing.

Retail sentiment around ZEC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘low’ chatter levels over the past day.

Grants Fight Keeps Growing

ZCG is a five-person committee that receives 8% of each Zcash block reward. Another 12% is put into a fund voted on by ZEC holders every quarter.

The latest round kicked off last week, led by Sean Bowe, co-founder of Zcash. He published a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) to disable ZCG’s 8% stream. The draft would send that share to the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM), a reserve within the protocol used to support future mining rewards. Bowe’s draft mentioned ZCG’s own dashboard that had about 91,453 ZEC. That's about $112 million in today's dollars.

ZCG countered with an offer of its own. The committee posted on a Zcash community forum, proposing to move 36,200 ZEC to the NSM and keep about 55,200 ZEC for grants. It admitted its 8% stake was more than necessary and said the plan was preliminary.

Critics say that won’t do.

On Friday, Cameron Winklevoss tweeted on X that the committee should be replaced by voting by coinholders.

The same day, Josh Swihart, founder of Zcash developer ZODL, took it a step further. “It’s time to kill the Zcash Dev Fund,” he wrote. Adding to it, he said, “Though I think the dev fund should end, I'm not opposed to this proposal. It's a reasonable compromise.”

All the plans are still drafts. Changing the block reward split will need a network upgrade.

Zcash has gained nearly 150% so far this year and is up over 214% in the last 12 months.

data.title: 5 key money rule changes from tomorrow, 1 November 2026: What pensioners, taxpayers and bank customers should know
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Several financial and banking-related changes will take effect from 1 November 2026. These include changes to GST provisions, revised bank charges and the annual life certificate submission window for pensioners.

Meanwhile, eligible taxpayers have a revised deadline for filing income tax returns. Here is what taxpayers, business owners, and bank account customers should know.

Government pensioners below 80 years of age can submit their annual life certificates from 1 November to 30 November 2026. Pensioners aged 80 and above have already started submitting them from 1 October.

They can submit the certificate physically at a pension-disbursing bank branch or digitally through the Jeevan Pramaan facility using Aadhaar-based authentication and face authentication.

PFRDA has also enabled the UPS Jeewan Setu Digital Life Certificate (DLC) facility for Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) subscribers. Eligible pensioners need to submit their annual life certificates through the Protean eGov App by 30 November.

The deadline for filing income tax returns for certain taxpayers covered under audit requirements for Assessment Year 2026-27 has been extended from 31 October to 21 November 2026.

The extension applies to eligible businesses, professionals, firms, and other specified taxpayers who have filed an tax audit report by 21 October 2026.

The government has notified changes to certain provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, effective 1 November 2026.

The amendments cover post-supply discounts, credit notes and GST refunds. They include revised conditions for excluding eligible post-sale discounts from taxable value, including the requirement to reverse attributable input tax credit.

The changes also address refund provisions, including those relevant to businesses facing inverted duty structures.

Punjab National Bank (PNB) has revised service charges on its Visa and RuPay credit card variants from 1 November 2026.

For cash withdrawals at PNB ATMs, the fee will be 2.5% of the amount withdrawn or Rs.400, whichever is higher. At other domestic ATMs, the charge will be 2.5% of the withdrawal amount or Rs.500, whichever is higher.

The bank has also revised late payment fees based on the outstanding amount due. Earlier, no charge was applied for dues of Rs.1,000 or less, while the maximum fee was Rs.750 for dues above Rs.10,000. From November 1, no fee will apply for dues up to Rs.500, while the maximum charge will increase to Rs.1,200 for outstanding amounts above Rs.50,000.

Additionally, PNB has introduced a utility bill payment fee of 1% of the total utility payments if they exceed Rs.50,000 in a billing cycle, subject to a maximum charge of Rs.2,000 per transaction. Earlier, no such fee was applicable.

Other changes on these credit cards include cheque return charges and ECS/auto-debit dishonour charges.

From 1 November, IndusInd Bank will levy charges on certain failed transactions for customers holding Indus Delite, Indus Digi-start, Indus Online-Min Bal Required and Indie (Star/ Superstar/ Megastar) savings accounts.

A POS transaction declined due to insufficient funds will now attract a Rs.25 charge. A failed IndusInd Bank ATM transaction due to insufficient balance will also cost Rs.25. Cheques returned for reasons other than financial reasons will attract a charge of Rs.50 per cheque.

These charges are exclusive of GST. Earlier, all three failed transaction types were free of charge.

data.title: Blockchain investigator Chainalysis hit by cybersecurity incident
data.description:
Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis said it was targeted in a cybersecurity incident, similar to those suffered recently by other platforms.

“Based on the investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to investigation content, authentication credentials, or session tokens,” it said in a blog post on Friday. Some non-sensitive customer data was exposed.

Chainalysis said it had engaged world-class third-party cybersecurity experts and was using large language models to support a review of its security and strengthen its defenses.

The company added that the security incident was not related to the recent crypto theft at Binance.

Cointelegraph reported on Thursday that Chainalysis had mapped out a network of Russian intermediaries that helped North Korean IT workers cash out millions of dollars in cryptocurrency.

Chainalysis posted on X on Friday that suspected North Korea-linked hacks accounted for almost 89% of reported crypto hack losses this year, up from 15% in 2021.

data.title: OpenAI IPO Valuation Target Reportedly Trimmed By $150B After Nasdaq 100 Registers Worst Month Since March 2025 Following Brutal Tech Sell-Off
data.description:
Key points:
  • OpenAI had been seeking to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, after pointing to a sharp increase in revenue since July to justify nearly doubling its valuation from $852 billion.
  • The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% Friday, while the index registered its worst month since March 2025, adding pressure to companies tied to the AI trade.
  • The report added that one OpenAI backer said that the fundraising process had begun amid enthusiasm for AI but was caught by a sharp reversal in the market.

OpenAI has reportedly cut its target for its latest funding round by $10 billion as the ChatGPT maker faces a tougher market backdrop and growing investor scrutiny of AI spending.

According to a report by The Financial Times citing people familiar with the matter, OpenAI is now seeking about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from its earlier target of $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation.

OpenAI Tempers Ambitions

OpenAI had been seeking to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, after pointing to a sharp increase in revenue since July to justify nearly doubling its valuation from $852 billion.

But the company has since tempered its ambitions, with the report stating that OpenAI had set Friday as the deadline for investors to commit to the round. The initial close was expected to bring in less than $20 billion after some investors reduced their allocations, according to the report.

A consortium of investment groups from the United Arab Emirates, including state-backed technology fund MGX, is expected to be the largest participant. As part of the deal, OpenAI would have an option to lease newly developed computing power in the region, according to the report.

Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz, along with SoftBank, also plan to participate, the report said. OpenAI raised $122 billion in March.

Tech Sell-Off Puts AI Spending Under The Microscope

The fundraising reset comes after a sharp sell-off in technology stocks and growing concerns about the pace and scale of AI spending.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% Friday, while the index registered its worst month since March 2025, adding pressure to companies tied to the AI trade. The Nasdaq 100 index closed lower by 6.65% in October, its worst month since March 2025 when it fell 7.69%.

The report added that one OpenAI backer said that the fundraising process had begun amid enthusiasm for AI but was caught by a sharp reversal in the market.

The company is also facing competition for investor attention from Anthropic, which is preparing for an IPO next month at a valuation of $1.5 trillion or more.

Ives, Damodaran Weigh In On Anthropic IPO Risks

The Anthropic IPO could add another complication for OpenAI as investors weigh the two AI companies at the same time.

During an interview with CNBC, Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives described the environment around Anthropic as a “perfect storm moment,” saying the company is “so key to this AI revolution build out.”

Ives continued to see a potential $1.5 trillion valuation for Anthropic despite the concerns. However, he acknowledged that Anthropic’s fundraising needs could put it “a bit in the penalty box” as AI companies compete for capital to fund infrastructure.

NYU Stern professor Aswath Damodaran focused on the market mood heading into the IPO.

“IPOs are all about mood and momentum,” Damodaran said, warning that the current environment could hurt Anthropic’s initial reception. He also described Anthropic, OpenAI and other parts of the AI ecosystem as deeply interconnected.

“They’re all connected at the hip. If one falls, they drag the others down with them,” Damodaran warned.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, declined 1.77%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) fell 3.47%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) closed lower by 1.07%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: Eveready Industries posts ₹31.92 cr profit in Q2 FY27
data.description:
Battery and flashlight maker Eveready Industries India Ltd on Saturday reported a consolidated net profit of ₹31.92 crore for the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis.

The company had posted a net loss of ₹7.91 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from the Burman family-promoted firm.

Its revenue from operations increased 10.72 per cent to ₹428.24 crore in the September quarter of FY27. It was at ₹386.78 crore in the corresponding quarter in the year-ago period.

The total expenses of Eveready Industries went up 11.93 per cent to ₹391.54 crore in the September quarter.

Eveready Industries' total income, which includes other income, was at ₹431.5 crore, up 11.48 per cent in the September quarter.

Chief Executive Officer Anirban Banerjee said, "Our eighth consecutive quarter of revenue growth reflects the strength of the business and gives us confidence in sustaining this progress. Alkaline batteries and rechargeable products remain important growth drivers, while portable Liquid vaporisers expand our mosquito protection portfolio, supported by the launch of the 'Unplug and use anywhere campaign'."

"Our focus remains on strengthening the product portfolio, expanding market presence and driving sustainable growth," he said.

It has also reduced its net debt, which was at ₹153 crore on September 30, 2026. It was at ₹164 crore at Q1 FY27.

"Looking ahead, Eveready remains focused on scaling up the Alkaline portfolio, building adoption of liquid vaporisers, and other rechargeable products. Higher input costs remain a watchpoint. The company will continue to review pricing in line with input cost movements while progressing the Jammu facility ramp-up," it said.

data.title: Is Equitas SFB stock fall after CEO a market overreaction? Here's what Envision’s Nilesh Shah thinks
data.description:
Equitas Small Finance Bank's recent 30% stock plunge following the resignation of Founder and Chief Executive Officer PN Vasudevan appears to be a market overreaction, according to Nilesh Shah, Founder, Envision Capital.

The stock corrected from ₹70 to around ₹50, wiping out nearly ₹2,000 crore in market capitalisation and dragging the bank's overall valuation below ₹6,000 crore. Vasudevan stepped down, citing a conflict-of-interest overhang, as his daughter is a co-promoter at another non-banking financial company (NBFC). He stated the decision aims to unlock the bank's real value and ensure longer-term value creation.

Shah noted that having a family member lead another NBFC is not inherently problematic, provided there are no undisclosed dealings. "I just feel that probably the market seems to have overreacted," he said.

Vasudevan confirmed to CNBC-TV18 that his decision is final and he will not reverse course, adding that the bank will now search for a successor. He assured that long-term growth, asset quality, and the return on assets (ROA) ratio remain on track, with no hidden issues expected to emerge.

Initial knee-jerk selloffs following sudden leadership changes have shown mixed recovery trajectories in the past. For instance, following the resignation of Girish Kousgi, the associated stock (PNB Housing Finance) fell around 17% before rallying 30% higher than its pre-announcement level.

Similarly, Navin Fluorine shares dropped up to 20% on the resignation of Managing Director and CEO Radhesh Welling but have since surged close to 120% from 2023 to date. Conversely, Cyient shares corrected 20% on a similar announcement and remained down by the same margin.

Watch the full conversation here

Separately, when asked to identify a winning market theme between now and next summer, Shah strongly favoured the "new economy," specifically highlighting consumer fintech, healthcare, and technology-powered businesses.

"Just spot that which business has the DNA of technology, innovation. I think they will be the disruptors, they will be the champions, they'll be the Sikandars (winners)," Shah said.

data.title: Waaree Energies denies pollution allegations at Gujarat plant
data.description:
Waaree Energies Ltd denied on Saturday October 31, that its South Gujarat factory polluted a village stream, calling the allegations “factually unsubstantiated” and demanding that the publisher, Mint, withdraw the report.

Waaree Energies Denies Allegations

The company said the water it released was harmless, a claim that matters because the stream runs through farmland and joins a river.

“The water discharge referenced in these reports consists of non-hazardous Reverse Osmosis reject wastewater,” the company said in a statement. Reverse osmosis is a water-purification method.

The company said its wastewater came only from clean drinking water and canteen food preparation and stayed within controlled environmental limits.

Waaree said it cooperated fully with the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) during every investigation, technical audit and field inspection. “We implemented every compliance requirement, successfully passed fair audits, and received complete official clearances,” the company said.

It added that plant leadership never received a complaint from local residents, and that its community relations team was now contacting villagers directly.

The statement followed a Mint report published on Thursday, October 29, which alleged that the factory had been releasing untreated industrial water straight into the Chanandevi stream.

The stream cuts through Sunthwad village in Chikhli taluka, Navsari, in South Gujarat’s agricultural belt. Just outside the village, it merges into the Vanganiya river, a tributary of the Ambika river.

Waaree Asks For Withdrawal Of Report

Waaree accused the publication of reporting what it called “minor, initial-stage operational adjustments” during rapid expansion. The company said any such instances were “negligible”, non-hazardous and resolved immediately. It argued that the coverage created panic and mistrust among villagers and workers who depend on the plant for their livelihoods.

Waaree asked the publication to withdraw the post immediately, saying the report relied on “unsubstantiated claims despite official regulatory clearances”.

The shares of the company closed 0.60% lower at the end of trade on Friday, October 30. The stock has registered losses of 22.04% in the year-to-date period while falling another 32.87% in the trailing 12-month period.

data.title: Tilaknagar Industries Q2 profit down 57.7% to ₹22 cr
data.description:
Homegrown spirits maker Tilaknagar Industries Ltd (TIL) on Friday reported a 57.7 per cent decline in consolidated net profit to ₹22.26 crore for the September quarter of FY27, mainly due to exceptional expenses related to integrating its Imperial Blue business.

The company had reported a net profit of ₹52.67 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Tilaknagar Industries Ltd (TIL) on Friday.

Tilaknagar Industries reported an exceptional loss of ₹10.94 crore during the quarter due to non-recurring expenses incurred in connection with integrating the Imperial Blue business division acquired from Pernod Ricard India.

Its profit before exceptional items and tax was ₹33.24 crore, down 37.16 per cent from ₹52.91 crore a year earlier.

This was led by volume, which "grew 160 per cent y-o-y, to reach 8.9 million cases (9 litre each)", the company said in its earnings statement.

TIL's revenue from operations was up twofold at ₹2,437.55 crore in the September quarter. It was at ₹896.92 crore in the year-ago period.

Similarly, total expenses of TIL were also up twofold at ₹2,405.08 crore in the second quarter of FY27.

Total income of TIL, which includes other income, was also up twofold at ₹2,438.33 crore in the September quarter.

Chairman & Managing Director Amit Dahanukar said, "While primary volumes in Q2 have remained flattish, our secondary volumes have remained robust and shown an impressive 8 per cent growth on q-o-q basis with Imperial Blue secondaries growing at 8.5 per cent and existing business secondaries growing at 7 per cent."

Imperial Blue has further strengthened its position with a pan-India market share gain of 100bps+ during the quarter, he added.

TIL is the maker of Mansion House Brandy, India's largest and the world's second-largest-selling brandy and home to Imperial Blue Whisky, the world's third-largest-selling whisky.

data.title: Indian travellers move beyond New Year parties, seek cultural, adventure and spiritual holidays: Thomas Cook India
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Indian travellers are increasingly looking beyond traditional New Year's Eve parties and celebrations, opting for holidays that combine cultural experiences, outdoor adventures, cruises and spiritual journeys, according to a press release issued by Thomas Cook (India) Limited and SOTC Travel.

The travel companies said that year-end holiday preferences are changing, with travellers seeking experiences that go beyond the midnight countdown, including Northern Lights excursions in Europe, cultural celebrations in Japan, premium island holidays and pilgrimage trips within India.

"New Year travel is increasingly about combining the excitement of celebration with the opportunity to discover a destination and its experiences," said Rajeev Kale, President and Country Head - Holidays, MICE and Visa, Thomas Cook (India) Limited.

He said Indian travellers are looking to make the occasion memorable through different experiences, ranging from watching New Year fireworks over Sydney Harbour to exploring European festive markets and Alpine landscapes.

"Indian travellers are looking to make the occasion memorable through distinctive experiences, whether it is watching the New Year fireworks over Sydney Harbour, exploring Europe's festive markets and Alpine landscapes, experiencing multiple destinations on a cruise or choosing a premium island escape like Lakshadweep or a spiritual journey in India," Kale said.

According to the companies' release, destinations such as Finland, Norway, Sweden and Iceland are among the options for travellers seeking winter experiences, including Northern Lights viewing, husky and reindeer sledding, snowmobile excursions and stays in glass igloos.

Japan is another destination being highlighted for its traditional New Year customs, including Hatsumode, the first shrine or temple visit of the year, while Southeast Asian destinations offer cultural experiences alongside festive celebrations.

Closer to home, spiritual tourism is also gaining momentum, with travellers seeking faith-based experiences during the year-end holiday season.

The companies said pilgrimage destinations such as Char Dham, Mahakaleshwar Temple in Ujjain, Tirupati and Vaishno Devi continue to attract travellers looking to combine holidays with prayer and reflection.

Premium island holidays are also emerging as an option for domestic travellers. Thomas Cook India and SOTC Travel have introduced direct charter flights from Bengaluru to Lakshadweep for the year-end season to make the island destination more accessible.

Cruises are another option for travellers seeking to combine New Year celebrations with visits to multiple destinations, with itineraries covering Southeast Asia, the Middle East, the Mediterranean and Australia-New Zealand.

SD Nandakumar, President and Country Head - Holidays and Corporate Tours, SOTC Travel, said travellers are increasingly seeking to make their holidays more meaningful through different activities and experiences.

"While New Year celebrations remain an important draw, travellers are also looking to make the most of their trips through local traditions, seasonal attractions, outdoor adventures, unique stays and cruise journeys," he said.

The companies said they are offering group tours and customised holiday packages across domestic and international destinations to cater to these varied travel preferences.

data.title: NTPC Q2 net profit jumps 39% to Rs 7,030 crore, revenue rises 21%
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- State-owned power major NTPC Limited reported a 38.7 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit attributable to shareholders to Rs 7,029.56 crore for the July-September quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2 FY27), compared with Rs 5,066.78 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The company's consolidated revenue from operations increased 21.2 per cent to Rs 54,269.95 crore from Rs 44,784.05 crore a year earlier, according to its unaudited financial results filed with the stock exchanges on Saturday.

NTPC's consolidated financial statement reported "Profit attributable to owners of the parent company" at Rs 7,029.56 crore, while total consolidated profit, including non-controlling interests, stood at Rs 7,350.79 crore, compared with Rs 5,225.30 crore in the year-ago period.

The company's total income rose to Rs 54,715.69 crore from Rs 45,262.10 crore, while total expenses increased to Rs 48,059.30 crore from Rs 40,218.03 crore.

Fuel costs increased to Rs 28,628.19 crore from Rs 23,062.34 crore during the same period.

The financial results also showed higher revenue from solar power generation and electricity trading.

According to the results, revenue from solar power stations increased to Rs 1,138.23 crore from Rs 722.52 crore a year earlier.

The company stated that revenue from operations included Rs 3,172.14 crore "on account of sale of energy through trading (gross)", compared with Rs 2,655.43 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

On a standalone basis, NTPC reported a 14.3 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 5,319.94 crore from Rs 4,653.33 crore a year earlier.

The company's board also declared its first interim dividend of Rs 3 per equity share for FY27.

The company fixed November 6, 2026, as the record date for the dividend, with payments scheduled to commence from November 25, 2026.

data.title: Aditya Birla Lifestyle Q2 result: Revenue rises; wholesale channel grows 18%
data.description:
Aditya Birla Lifestyle reported its results for Q2FY27 on Thursday, October 31. The retailer improved its figures from FY26, reporting an increase in profit and revenue.

Aditya Birla Lifestyle Q2

The Mumbai-based retailer reported a net profit of ₹53 crore for the quarter that ended in September, higher than the previous year's ₹23 crore (YoY). When it comes to its topline figure, the company's revenue for Q2 came in at ₹2,266 crore, compared to ₹2,038 crore last year, marking a 11.2% rise.

When it comes to its operational profitability, the company reported Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortisation, or EBITDA, up 13.8% from the previous year, as it posted EBITDA of ₹360 crore, compared to ₹317 crore in the previous year. Finally, the company reported a margin of 15.9%, marginally higher than 15.5% in Q2FY26.

Business Breakdown For Q2

Delving deeper into the company's business, the Lifestyle Brands business grew revenue 9% to ₹1,906 crore from ₹1,754 crore. Its EBITDA rose to ₹371 crore from ₹338 crore, and its margin edged up to 19.5% from 19.3%.

Meanwhile, the Emerging Business segment grew faster, with revenue up 27% to ₹371 crore from ₹292 crore. Its EBITDA jumped to ₹25 crore from ₹4 crore, lifting its margin to 6.8% from 1.5%. Inter-segment eliminations were ₹11 crore on revenue, against ₹8 crore last year, and ₹6 crore on EBITDA, against ₹5 crore.

In terms of channels of revenue, retail, the largest channel, grew 8% to ₹1,209 crore from ₹1,123 crore. Wholesale was the fastest-growing channel, up 18% to ₹597 crore from ₹506 crore. E-commerce rose 12% to ₹360 crore from ₹322 crore, and other channels grew 15% to ₹99 crore from ₹86 crore.

Furthermore, as of September 2026, the company operates 3,434 brand stores across more than 800 cities and towns. This includes over 560 stores in small towns and a presence in more than 190 malls. The company’s retail footprint stands at 5.1 million sq ft.

Stock Performance

When we look at the performance of the company's stock, it fell nearly 1% on Friday's trade, taking it closer to ₹70 per share. The stock has fallen over 30% in the past 6 months, and over 44% in this year's trade.

data.title: Russia extends diesel export ban until end of January, government says
data.description:
Russia has extended a ban on exports of diesel by producers through January 31, 2027, the government said on Saturday.

The government said the measure was aimed at maintaining stability on the domestic fuel market.

data.title: Virgin Media O2 to cut thousands of jobs, Sky News reports
data.description:
British telecoms operator Virgin Media O2, which is jointly owned by Liberty Global and Spain's Telefonica , will cut thousands of jobs in a sweeping shakeup, Sky News reported on Saturday, citing people close to the company.

  • Up to 4,000 of Virgin Media O2's 16,000 employees could be affected, although the precise number of job cuts has yet to be finalised, the report said

  • Most of the job cuts are expected to affect non-customer-facing roles, while a number of senior leadership changes are already under way, the report said

  • Virgin Media O2 declined to comment on the report

  • The company is also expected to review usage of contractors and suppliers in an effort to reduce costs, the report said

  • The Financial Times reported in July that VMO2's owners were weighing options to reduce the company's £22 billion ($29.46 billion) debt pile

  • In September, the Financial Times reported Virgin Media O2’s shareholders were seeking to reduce costs by about £600 million

($1 = 0.7468 pounds)

data.title: NTPC Q2 results: Standalone profit rises 14%, beats estimates; declares ₹3 interim dividend
data.description:
Integrated Power Utility firm NTPC reported a 14.3% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to ₹5,320 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared to ₹4,653 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Profit was higher than the CNBC-TV18 poll estimate of ₹5,031 crore.

Revenue from operations rose 16.8% year-on-year to ₹45,752 crore from ₹39,165 crore, also beating the CNBC-TV18 poll estimate of ₹43,192 crore.

Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) increased 8.7% to ₹10,891 crore from ₹10,018 crore a year ago. However, it missed the poll estimate of ₹12,393 crore.

EBITDA margin stood at 24% against 26% in the year-ago quarter, also below the CNBC-TV18 poll estimate of 29%.

Declares ₹3 interim dividend

NTPC's board has declared a first interim dividend of 30%, or ₹3 per equity share, on the face value of ₹10 for FY27.

The company has fixed November 6, 2026, as the record date for determining shareholders eligible for the interim dividend.

Capex and fixed assets

NTPC Group's gross fixed assets stood at ₹4,85,444 crore as of September 30, 2026, compared to ₹4,37,142 crore a year ago.

Group capital expenditure during H1 FY27 stood at ₹23,932 crore, against ₹23,115 crore in H1 FY26.

Pumped storage and battery storage plans

NTPC Group has a pumped storage project (PSP) portfolio of 16 GW. Of this, the 1 GW Tehri PSP project of THDC is under commercial operation, while detailed project reports for other projects with a combined capacity of 15 GW are in progress.

The company is also working on 5 GWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity allocated under the Viability Gap Funding scheme of the Power System Development Fund. The capacity is planned across 15 NTPC thermal power stations and one group company, with commissioning expected to commence from June 2027 onwards.

Meanwhile, the NGEL Group is executing 1,620 MWh of BESS projects, with an additional 40 GWh of projects under tendering and planning.

Progress on nuclear energy plans

NTPC Parmanu Urja Nigam Limited (NPUNL), a wholly owned subsidiary, has identified 30 potential sites across multiple states for nuclear projects.

Site selection studies have been completed at four locations, while studies are at an advanced stage at six other locations.

data.title: Talking Costco: Why a special dividend might not be the right play
data.description:
Costco is widely anticipated to be close to teeing up a special dividend. The retailer started paying special dividends in December 2012 with a one-time payout of $7 per share, which cost about $3B. After that, the company paid $5 per share in February 2015 and $7 per share in May 2017. In November 2020, the board declared a $10 per share special dividend, and the largest one so far was the $6.7B payout in January 2024.

While some analysts and income-loving shareholders are expecting the next special dividend in 2027, Mizuho analyst David Bellinger asked whether the capital could be deployed more strategically elsewhere.

Bellinger and his team think Costco is definitively behind others when it comes to e-commerce operations, rapid fulfillment, and retail media. "We believe management could address certain weaknesses and decelerating membership growth by re-routing what would likely be $8B to 9B from a special dividend back into the business," highlighted Bellinger.

Specifically, Bellinger thinks Costco could use the funds to ramp up digital investments centered around rapid delivery options for groceries, as well as building out several hundred standalone gas stations to fuel member growth and solidify retention rates. Currently, Costco has one standalone gas station open in Mission Viejo, California, and has plans to build one in Honolulu.

In addition, the Mizuho analysts believe acquiring a high-margin advertising arm similar to what Walmart has done with VIZIO and Vibe.co could stoke future growth and margins, as well as create pushback against the bearish narrative of under-investment by the Issaquah, Washington-based company.

data.title: The 10-Point: America's Debt Soars as Washington's Fiscal Hawks Vanish — WSJ Newsletter
data.description:
Emma Tucker

1. FROM MY DESK

Something is missing from this year's midterm campaigns: America's soaring debt. In 2018, 140 political ads mentioned the debt or deficit. This year, just 30 have.

The silence is striking. Federal debt held by the public reached 100% of GDP for the first time in 80 years, while interest costs now exceed military spending. Yet the politicians once willing to sound the alarm-the fiscal hawks-have largely vanished.

What happened? Some retired, lost elections or simply changed the subject. Rising debt without a financial-market revolt robbed hawks of credibility and made prominent economists rethink the conventional wisdom on debt. Richard Rubin and David Luhnow examine how Washington stopped worrying about debt-and what it could cost us. And with Election Day just three days away, follow our live coverage for the latest developments and analysis.

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you're not subscribed, sign up here. If you're reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES

  • With disquieting signals of widespread losses in the midterms, the mood among Republicans is grim, and they are scrambling to play defense even in some seats previously seen as GOP strongholds.
  • Polling and politics editor Aaron Zitner breaks down the last WSJ poll before the elections, which shows that 60% of the 1,500 voters we surveyed want the next Congress to be a check on Trump's power during his final two years in office.
  • OpenAI has raised less than half of the $30 billion it had initially targeted for its latest funding round, with market jitters over the AI trade dampening investor appetite.
  • Affordable Care Act plan premiums will rise by 13% in 2027, the second straight year of double-digit increases.
  • Christine Lagarde, the departing European Central Bank leader, is wagering that her brand of politics still has a place in a world increasingly driven by polarization.

3. FROM THE MARKETS

  • In the latest, and biggest, cyberattack on the crypto industry, North Korean hackers ransacked Binance, making off with $6.3 billion in just 20 minutes. Read the inside story of the record-breaking heist that became crypto's biggest nightmare.
  • The cracks in the AI trade multiplied through the week, culminating in a tech selloff Friday that sent the Nasdaq composite to its worst day since June.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST

How Iran battered U.S. bases and caused billions in damage.

Iran's missile campaign against U.S. forces in the Middle East took a turn in July when the regime shifted tactics: Tehran began taking more direct aim at the buildings American troops lived and slept in. The Pentagon has said little publicly about the destruction. But U.S. military installations have lost critical defense systems and suffered billions in damage, and Iranian attacks have forced the U.S. to move troops off several bases. By analyzing tens of thousands of satellite images, the Journal identified hundreds of damaged buildings across more than two dozen installations-offering the most comprehensive public accounting of the war's damage to American facilities to date.

  • Read about how our reporters conducted the investigation.

5.

Why cheap money is drying up for the AI build-out.

For years, the companies behind America's artificial-intelligence boom have raised hundreds of billions of dollars with ease. Now, the balance of power is shifting. Lenders and investors are getting choosier about where to place their bets and are demanding tougher terms, signaling a new phase in the AI build-out. Disappointing earnings reports from technology companies this week prompted a rout in AI-related stocks and bonds, leading Friday to one of the biggest market selloffs since AI-mania began, report Peter Rudegeair, Robbie Whelan and Jack Pitcher.

Make sense of AI's impact on business. Sign up for WSJ AI & Business, a free weekly newsletter packed with news, insights and data from our global team of technology journalists.

6. SEE THE STORY

This is the most important chart in AI, and you probably haven't seen it before.

Published by Anthropic, the chart shows how much of its AI research and development is being done by AI. As recently as March, AI led only 1% of that research. By August, it was leading 26%. As this technology accelerates its own evolution, the risk is that we struggle to keep pace and keep it under control, writes columnist Ben Cohen.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

  • Saturday: Trick-or-treaters take to the streets for Halloween. The Atlanta Dream face the Golden State Valkyries in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals.
  • Sunday: Daylight-saving time ends. The New York City Marathon takes place. Formula One's Mexico City Grand Prix is held, and the National Women's Soccer League wraps up its regular season, finalizing the playoff bracket.
  • Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER

$1 billion

That's the annual sales generated by Goldfish, making it one of Campbell's four biggest brands. But the company's sales are falling and its stock has slipped 29% over the past year. Eating habits have changed. People aren't eating as much canned soup and packaged snacks. To appeal to parents, the company has embarked on a five-year quest to reinvent the Goldfish, including by making a gluten-free option of the popular children's snack.

9. AND FINALLY...

Surf communities are selling big waves to homeowners-no ocean required.

Instead of golf courses, ski mountains or lakes, high-end housing developments are offering surfing as the main activity. Thanks to advances in wave-pool technology, man-made surf lagoons are becoming the latest amenity developers are using to lure buyers. But the luxury doesn't come cheap: Capital costs reach up to $350 million for one lagoon with a surf deck.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

  • Opinion: Disappointing earnings reports triggered a selloff in tech and AI shares, while Binance reported hackers pilfered $6.3 billion.
  • WSJ | Buy Side: Don't be fooled by misinformation that often passes as "common wisdom" about car insurance.

ABOUT US

The 10-Point is your guide to The Wall Street Journal's reporting and analysis you can't get anywhere else. Your subscription makes our journalism possible.

data.title: After Welcomhotel Manesar, ITC Hotels expands Delhi-NCR presence with 105-key Fortune Select Greater Noida
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- ITC Hotels Limited has signed a management agreement for the 105-key Fortune Select Greater Noida under its Asset Right strategy, expanding the Fortune brand footprint across the National Capital Region (NCR) and Uttar Pradesh.

According to ITC Hotels, Fortune Select Greater Noida will feature contemporary rooms and suites, an all-day dining restaurant, banqueting facilities and a range of amenities designed to offer guests a comfortable and convenient stay.

The facility, which also has amenities tailored primarily for corporate guests and MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions) events, is slated to open early next year.

"Greater Noida is a strategic addition to Fortune brand's growing portfolio. It is a high-impact market, driven by growing industrial activity, recurring MICE demand, strong NCR corporate connectivity, and the growth impetus of the Jewar Airport corridor," Anil Chadha, Managing Director of ITC Hotels Limited, said in a release.

"We see significant potential for quality branded hospitality in this market, and Fortune Select Greater Noida is well positioned to add value by bringing its signature hospitality to meet the evolving needs of business and leisure travellers alike," he added.

The property will be situated within the India Expo Plaza at Knowledge Park II, a flagship mixed-use development in the region.

With the addition of Fortune Select Greater Noida, Fortune will have a presence across five hotels in Uttar Pradesh and five hotels in the NCR, further consolidating its network across the region.

"We are pleased to collaborate with the Fortune brand which is backed by the legacy and iconic hospitality expertise of ITC Hotels Limited. The hotel will be located within India Expo Plaza at Knowledge Park II, Greater Noida, our flagship mixed-use development and most premium project," Ankur Mittal, Chairman and Managing Director of SVG Realty and Vinayaka Expo Plaza Private Limited, said.

"As Greater Noida continues to strengthen its position as a leading business and commercial hub in the NCR, we look forward to contributing to the region's evolving hospitality landscape and welcoming business, MICE, and leisure travellers to Fortune Select Greater Noida," Mittal added.

Earlier this month, ITC Hotels Ltd announced the signing of a 104-key Welcomhotel in Manesar, Gurugram.

Anil Chadha, Managing Director, ITC Hotels, said, "As hospitality demand continues to evolve beyond traditional gateway cities, we remain focused on identifying destinations that offer strong long-term growth potential. Welcomhotel in Manesar is a strategic addition to our portfolio, bringing together a high-growth location, robust connectivity, and a thriving events market."

"The hotel's connectivity to key economic centres located in Delhi, Gurugram, Noida and Faridabad will enable it to capture growing demand from both corporate and social segments, while offering a less congested and more destination-oriented environment," ITC Hotels said in a statement.

ITC Hotels currently has a presence across India, Sri Lanka and Nepal through a portfolio of more than 155 properties and over 14,200 keys.

data.title: Bangladesh death toll from dengue rises, unlikely to ease before December
data.description:
By Ruma Paul

Bangladesh recorded its highest monthly dengue death toll of the year in October, with experts warning the outbreak is unlikely to ease significantly before December.

The outbreak has killed 418 people and led to more than 133,000 hospital admissions this year as of October 30, according to health ministry data. October alone accounted for 173 deaths, surpassing September's 148 and making it the deadliest month of 2026 so far.

The surge comes as Bangladesh is also battling the world's worst measles outbreak, which has killed more than 1,200 people, placing additional strain on an already stretched healthcare system.

HOSPITALS UNDER PRESSURE

Doctors said many dengue patients were only seeking hospital admission after developing severe complications. At the state-run Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College and Hospital in Dhaka, 279 dengue patients were being treated after 67 new admissions in a single day, hospital director Mirza Golam Sarwar said.

"We are getting many patients in shock. Their blood pressure is sometimes too low to measure, and their oxygen levels are dropping," he said.

Medicine specialist ABM Abdullah said repeat infections and delays in diagnosis and treatment were driving severe cases and deaths.

"People who have had dengue before may face a greater risk of severe illness if they become infected again," he said, urging people to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and seek care as soon as symptoms appear.

Dhaka resident Faisal Ferdous, 33, was diagnosed with dengue in 2017, 2024 and again earlier this month. "This time, both my wife and I needed hospital treatment," said Ferdous, who is now at home recovering.

Ferdous said the couple fell ill shortly after spending several days at a hospital where their five-year-old son was being treated for an unrelated illness.

"Every bout has been difficult, and after getting it repeatedly, you become increasingly concerned about the risk of severe illness," he said.

Health experts warn that the circulation of all four dengue virus serotypes is increasing the risk of severe disease. People infected with one strain can later contract another, raising the likelihood of complications. Bangladesh has yet to introduce a dengue vaccine, although authorities are considering one as a longer-term measure.

CLIMATE CHANGE EXTENDS DENGUE SEASON

Entomologist Kabirul Bashar of Jahangirnagar University said deaths were unlikely to continue rising at October's pace, but transmission would probably persist through November.

"We may see some relief, but dengue is unlikely to disappear in November. Any decline is likely to be modest, with significant improvement unlikely before December," he said.

Bashar said mosquitoes would continue emerging from breeding sites created by earlier rainfall, sustaining transmission even as conditions become drier. Changing rainfall and humidity patterns, partly linked to climate change, were extending mosquito breeding seasons and keeping Aedes mosquitoes active for longer, he said.

data.title: Muthoot Finance Q2: Net profit rises 27% to ₹2,978 crore, NII up 34%; beats estimates
data.description:
Muthoot Finance reported a 27% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹2,978 crore for the second quarter FY27, compared to ₹2,345 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The profit figure was higher than the CNBC-TV18 poll estimate of ₹2,950 crore.

Net interest income (NII) rose 34.4% year-on-year to ₹5,365 crore from ₹3,992 crore a year ago, beating the CNBC-TV18 poll estimate of ₹4,525 crore.

H1 performance

For the half year ended September 30, 2026, consolidated loan assets under management (AUM) grew 42% year-on-year to ₹2,09,317 crore, while consolidated profit after tax (PAT) increased 39% to ₹6,103 crore, as per a press release filed at NSE.

Standalone loan AUM rose 42% to ₹1,87,810 crore, while standalone PAT increased 26% to ₹5,527 crore.

Consolidated gold loan AUM grew 46% year-on-year to ₹1,93,212 crore, while standalone gold loan AUM increased 43% to ₹1,78,956 crore.

The company added around 5 lakh active customers during the half year, taking the total to 69 lakh from 64 lakh. The quantity of gold held as security in its lockers increased to 204 tonnes from 196 tonnes.

Standalone gold loan disbursements to new customers stood at ₹20,238 crore, covering 9,93,900 customers during the half year.

Raises gold loan growth guidance

Commenting on the performance, Managing Director Alexander George Muthoot said the company was raising its gold loan growth guidance for FY27 by an additional 10%.

He added, "The RBI's updated gold lending guidelines, effective 1st April 2026, involves a learning curve for us as well as customers, which will get stabilized over few quarters irrespective of which growth trajectory will continue."

He said the company's standalone loan AUM reached ₹1,87,810 crore, registering 42% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter growth.

Subsidiaries report mixed performance

Belstar Microfinance reported a profit after tax of ₹144 crore in H1 FY27, compared to a loss of ₹160 crore in H1 FY26. Its loan AUM stood at ₹7,876 crore, marginally higher than ₹7,715 crore a year ago.

Gross non-performing assets (GNPA) improved to 3.26% from 4.58%, while net non-performing assets (NNPA) declined to 0.07% from 0.26%.

Collection efficiency improved to 99.61% from 99.25% during the same period. Belstar added 82 gold loan branches in H1 FY27, taking the total to 163, while its overall branch network increased to 1,362 from 1,287 a year ago. Its gold loan portfolio reached ₹484 crore.

Muthoot Homefin's loan AUM increased around 7% year-on-year to ₹3,460 crore in H1 FY27 from ₹3,247 crore. Interest income rose around 13% to ₹202 crore from ₹179 crore, while profit after tax increased around 9% to ₹11 crore from ₹10 crore.

Another subsidiary, Muthoot Money reported a 99% year-on-year increase in loan AUM to ₹12,716 crore in H1 FY27 from ₹6,393 crore. Total income rose around 120% to ₹1,103 crore from ₹500 crore, while profit after tax surged around 242% to ₹364 crore from ₹106 crore.

Board approves subsidiary merger

During the quarter, the board approved the merger of wholly-owned subsidiary Muthoot Money Limited with Muthoot Finance Limited, with April 1, 2027, as the appointed date, subject to regulatory and other approvals.

The company said the strategic consolidation would simplify the group structure and unlock combined operational and financial efficiencies.

Shares of Muthoot Finance ended 3.54% lower at ₹2,408.60 on the NSE on October 30.

data.title: Virgin Media O2 to cut thousands of jobs, Sky News reports
data.description:
British telecoms operator Virgin Media O2, which is jointly owned by Liberty Global and Spain's Telefonica , will cut thousands of jobs in a sweeping shakeup, Sky News reported on Saturday, citing people close to the company.

  • Up to 4,000 of Virgin Media O2's 16,000 employees could be affected, although the precise number of job cuts has yet to be finalised, the report said

  • Most of the job cuts are expected to affect non-customer-facing roles, while a number of senior leadership changes are already under way, the report said

  • Virgin Media O2 did not immediately respond to a request for comment

  • The company is also expected to review usage of contractors and suppliers in an effort to reduce costs, the report said

  • The Financial Times reported in July that VMO2's owners were weighing options to reduce the company's £22 billion ($29.46 billion) debt pile

  • In September, the Financial Times reported Virgin Media O2’s shareholders were seeking to reduce costs by about £600 million

($1 = 0.7468 pounds)

data.title: Eveready Industries Q2 result: Battery maker turns profitable YoY; margins slip
data.description:
Eveready Industries announced its results for the July to September quarter on Saturday, October 31. In this quarter, the company turned to profit compared to the previous year's loss; meanwhile, its margins contracted YoY.

Eveready Industries Q2

The battery manufacturer reported a net profit of ₹92 crore for the September quarter, against a net loss of ₹8 crore in the same period last year.

When it comes to the top-line figures, the Kolkata-based company reported revenue from operations of ₹428 crore, recording an 11% year-on-year increase from ₹387 crore a year earlier.

When it comes to its profitability, the numbers missed the mark compared to last cycle, as the Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortisation, or EBITDA, grew 3.6% to ₹50.7 crore from ₹49 crore. However, the EBITDA margin contracted to 12% from 13% a year ago.

Batteries accounted for 64% of the company's revenue this quarter, where it has category leadership. The Flashlights segment came in second, with 14% of all the revenue. In addition to that, the Lighting business brought in 22 % of the total revenue.

Q1 Results

Sequentially speaking, the company saw a year-on-year increase of 23.3% in net profit, reaching ₹37 crore for the first quarter of FY27, while operational revenue rose by 9% to ₹407.7 crore. EBITDA saw a year-on-year growth of 14%, amounting to ₹61.2 crore, with the EBITDA margin standing at 15%, in contrast to 14.3% from the previous year.

Company On Business Environment

In its statement, the company laid emphasis on value-conscious purchases and affordability remaining important amid uneven rural and urban demand.

According to the company, weak monsoon conditions led to moderation in the rural segment, while urban demand remained resilient. Amid the ongoing volatility in the global markets, elevated commodity costs continue to pose margin pressures across consumer businesses, the company added.

Furthermore, Eveready underscored that currency volatility and inflationary pressures reinforce the need for pricing and cost management and continued investment in distribution and supply chains, with a sharper focus on general trade expansion, modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce, and continued growth momentum.

When we take a quick look at the stock performance, the company's shares closed Friday's trade with losses of close to 3%. In the past year of trading, the company's shares have fallen 18.25%, taking the stock price to ₹310.55 per share.

data.title: Envision Capital's Nilesh Shah bets on OnEMI and Milky Mist for their strong growth potential
data.description:
Envision Capital is bullish on consumer financial technology platform OnEMI Technology Solutions and dairy company Milky Mist Dairy Food, driven by their strong growth metrics and differentiated business models, according to the Founder Nilesh Shah.

Discussing the financial sector, Shah highlighted OnEMI, which operates the product loan platform Kissht, as a "quick credit" business equipped with a robust technology stack that enables rapid loan processing. The company recently reported quarterly earnings showing a solid growth rate of 40-50%.

"I still believe that in the overall context, it's still kind of a small business, probably less than a billion dollars of assets under management (AUM)," Shah said. "Probably just about there and growing at a 40-50% growth rate, which is quite phenomenal. If they manage the credit cost well, who knows? I mean, this could be a phenomenal business."

He cautioned that as a credit business, it remains essential to monitor credit quality and costs, though he noted the company's leadership team has managed them well so far.

In the dairy sector, Envision Capital favours Milky Mist for its unique approach to the market. Unlike traditional milk companies that aim for 10-30% of their sales to come from value-added products, Milky Mist generates 100% of its revenue from this segment.

Shah described the company as "value-added native" and noted that the current regulatory push for high-quality products heavily favours such businesses.

Watch the full conversation here

"There's a huge shift from unorganised to organised, and that's probably just started," he said, adding that over the next five to 10 years, these companies have the potential to become significantly larger.
